title: What shaped India's economy: five measured outcomes
status: Evidence-based scorecard supporting the annual synthesis. Not a causal ranking and not the completed C18 flagship article.
method: Each row keeps its own observation period, source publication date and measurement vintage. Do not combine the indicators into an arbitrary weighted total. Source-specific descriptions take precedence over narrative labels.

dimensions.name: Household purchasing power
dimensions.question: How much did prices change, and for whom?

main.label: Headline CPI inflation
main.note: Both figures are year-on-year inflation rates, not the month-on-month change in the index.

dimensions.observed: MoSPI recorded provisional combined CPI inflation of 6.09% in October, with food inflation at 8.94% and higher rural headline inflation than urban. The variation matters for household expenditure burdens.
dimensions.mechanism: Different consumption baskets, food costs, fuel and transport changes can alter households' real purchasing power even when the national headline rate is identical.
dimensions.cannot_infer: This release does not tell us the distribution of real wage changes, the tax-cut pass-through to specific goods or which household suffered the largest welfare loss.
dimensions.next_test: Matched household expenditure weights, observed real earnings, commodity-level retail prices and consistent prior-period inflation vintages.

dimensions.name: Work and job quality
dimensions.question: Were more people working, and in what jobs?

main.label: PLFS unemployment rate
main.note: Age 15+, Current Weekly Status, all India; quarterly not monthly unemployment.

dimensions.observed: Overall unemployment declined to 5.1% from 5.4%; worker-population ratio increased to 52.7% from 51.7%. Rural self-employment expanded in the composition of work.
dimensions.mechanism: Rising participation and employment together change the interpretation of a falling unemployment rate. Job status and hours also affect income security.
dimensions.cannot_infer: The unemployment and employment ratios alone do not establish higher real wages, improved hours, formal employment or durable career progression.
dimensions.next_test: Comparable worker earnings, paid hours, contract security, urban/rural job transitions, cohort composition and confidence intervals.

dimensions.name: Growth and investment
dimensions.question: Did expansion represent productive investment?
dimensions.observed: Real GDP grew 7.8% and gross fixed capital formation grew 11.9% year on year in April–June. Consumption and fixed investment each contributed approximately four percentage points of measured growth on the expenditure side.
dimensions.mechanism: Stronger demand can make additional capacity attractive, but national accounts measure total investment by public, private and household sectors.
dimensions.cannot_infer: Total GFCF is not private corporate capital expenditure. A growth contribution is accounting, not an identified causal effect of a policy or project.
dimensions.next_test: Company and small-firm actual capital expenditure, project commissioning and utilisation, sector jobs and vintage-consistent GDP revisions.

dimensions.name: Public investment and fiscal capacity
dimensions.question: How much of the public investment plan was realised?

main.label: FY26 Union capital expenditure, provisional
main.note: The comparison is actual provisional outturn against an earlier plan, not two time-series observations.

dimensions.observed: CGA provisional, unaudited accounts recorded ₹10,69,119 crore in Union capital expenditure against the original ₹11,21,090 crore budget, a shortfall of ₹51,971 crore.
dimensions.mechanism: An allocation, a loan disbursement, a contractor payment, a commissioned asset and reliable user access are different stages of public capital formation.
dimensions.cannot_infer: The shortfall does not establish project inefficiency or failure. Spending does not establish completed roads, capacity utilised or private investment crowded in.
dimensions.next_test: Matched project awards, releases, construction milestones, physical asset commissioning and service quality, with final audited fiscal accounts.

primary.title: Controller General of Accounts FY2025–26 provisional accounts

dimensions.name: External resilience
dimensions.question: How did India pay for its goods deficit?

main.label: Current-account balance
main.note: Preliminary current vs partially revised comparison; both same half-year.

dimensions.observed: RBI reported a preliminary first-half current-account deficit of US$25.8bn, compared with a partially revised US$18.0bn deficit a year earlier. Services and transfers offset part of a larger net goods deficit.
dimensions.mechanism: Service exports and transfers create foreign-currency receipts; private and official financing transactions can fund the remaining current-account gap.
dimensions.cannot_infer: Financing inflows do not prove external sustainability, nor do recorded monetary movements capture changes in foreign exchange reserve stocks due to valuation.
dimensions.next_test: Maturity and currency composition of liabilities, cost of financing, reserve-cover definition and matching goods/services observations over several quarters.

primary.title: RBI September 2026 Balance of Payments release

editorial_decision: Do not assign a composite score or rank the five dimensions by subjective importance or incomparable numerical magnitudes. An annual flagship article is a separate editorial deliverable and should be published only after its mechanisms, comparisons and contrary evidence are verified.
